identity.description: Send a one-line brief, get three RENDERED page compositions back. A vision model decomposes curated reference designs into transferable composition principles (depth planes, overlaps, data pinned to imagery, container breaks) and transfers them onto YOUR product — then renders, structurally scores, critiques, and revises the winner. Ships a composition spec + positioned composition.html, a WCAG-solved theme.css, design kit, hero.png, and og.png.

inputs.description: What you are about to build. JSON {goal, vibe, framework, count} — or just a plain sentence like "playful waitlist page for a plant-care app". count picks how many references come back (2-8, default 4).

outputs.description: The design direction as markdown: which comp won and why, concrete build guidance, the three comps ranked with scores, and apply-in-order instructions.

Machine-readable design kit: provenance (composition source, reference id, signature patterns used, principles that survived the render, sanitizer repairs, critique rounds, deadline sheds), winner (tokens, palette, headline, hero source), all three directions with structural + domain + palette score parts, icons (inline SVG + npm imports), photo, pattern, matched refs, notes.

The build plan for the winning COMPOSITION: every element with its resolved percent geometry, depth plane, overlaps, pinned annotations, container breaks, imagery treatment, and custom viz primitives — derived from the composition spec, not from section recipes. The coding agent builds THIS, not its own habits.
Append-safe stylesheet for the winning direction: WCAG-solved custom properties plus element overrides. Link it after existing styles and it applies without refactoring.

Micro-animation kit tuned to the direction's energy: staggered scroll reveals, floating drift, hover lift/tilt, underline draw, scrolled-nav state — all wired via data-attributes, reduced-motion safe.
Dependency-free companion script for the motion kit (IntersectionObserver reveals, float phasing, pointer tilt). Load with defer.
Floating component assets rendered in the winning direction's real fonts and palette — stat chips, sticker badges, tag pills, mini-cards — as inline-ready SVG strings with brief-specific content.

Direction 1 (faithful transfer) as a rendered full-page composition preview — the actual page layout: depth planes, overlaps, pinned data, container breaks. Falls back to a 1200x1500 style tile when composition transfer was unavailable.
Direction 2 (bolder — transferred from the structurally richest matched reference), same rendering.
Direction 3 (unexpected — transferred from the most visually distant reference), same rendering.
All three comps side by side with scores, winner ringed — show this to the user before building.

The winning direction's 1024px hero image: the licensed bank photograph matched to the brief, gradient-mapped to the exact token palette (credit in kit.winner.heroCredit). Procedural gradient only when the bank has no match.
1200x630 og:image — the winner's hero under a scrim with the headline composited in the winning typeface.
A contact-sheet JPEG of the matched reference designs from the bank. Absent when the bank is empty or the embed sidecar is down.

The winning CompositionSpec plus its resolved pixel geometry: elements with roles, frames, depth planes, relations (overlaps / attachedTo / breaksContainer / offsetFrom / encircles), imagery treatments, viz drawing primitives, and the resolver's adjustment log. The machine-readable form of the design.

The winning composition serialized as standalone positioned HTML/CSS — identical geometry to the comp preview by construction (percent-positioned, z-index from depth planes, inline viz SVGs, data-role attributes). Port it into your framework instead of re-inventing the layout.

The winning reference's structural decomposition: visual masses with bounding boxes, depth planes and overlaps, imagery integration, data-display forms, and the signature patterns (observation + transferable principle) the transfer was built from.
